attribution.problem: The schedule is one expression naming eight hours, so GitHub reports the same expression for every slot and a run does not say which slot triggered it.
attribution.method: Each run is measured against the nearest cron slot at or before its createdAt. A run delayed past a later slot is credited to that later slot, so every delay below is a lower bound on the real one.
attribution.consequence: The delay figures understate the delay. They are not used to attribute any individual run to a slot, and no claim below depends on such an attribution.

lowerBoundDelayMinutes.definition: createdAt minus the nearest cron slot at or before it. startedAt equals createdAt on all 100 runs, so the queue time is the earliest instant the gate could have read.
lowerBoundDelayMinutes.createdWithin60MinutesIsAnUpperBound: A run credited to a later slot looks punctual. At most this many of the 100 were on time.

wallClockGateOutcome.designIntent: exactly four of every eight slots open, so 50 of 100
wallClockGateOutcome.note: This count needs no attribution: it is the gate's own predicate applied to each run's createdAt.

scheduledRunsCreatedPerUtcDay.note: GitHub created all eight through 2026-08-25 and four or fewer afterwards. Scheduled runs are best effort and may be dropped under load; this measurement cannot distinguish a dropped invocation from one never queued.

refreshOutcome.reason: scripts/wildfire/refresh.mjs throws 'No cleared live-wildfire feed is configured' before any external request, and the repository variable WILDFIRE_SOURCE_URLS was empty in every observed run. Every run the gate opened therefore failed. That is the fail-closed source-rights design working, not a scheduling fault.

observations: Created 2026-08-29T10:49:05Z, at least 349.1 minutes after the slot that triggered it.
The wall clock read 03:00 America/Vancouver, which is not one of the four required hours, so the gate logged run=false.

limitations: This is a time-bounded snapshot of the 100 most recent runs at retrieval time.
createdAt is GitHub's queue time, not the runner's start. Every delay here is a lower bound twice over.
The window lies entirely within Pacific daylight time. It does not observe a daylight saving transition.

Moving the cron minute off the hour mitigates delay and dropped invocations. It does not guarantee them: GitHub does not promise scheduled delivery, so four refreshes a day cannot be asserted from this repository's code alone.
Nothing here shows a successful refresh. No live wildfire feed has cleared source rights, so the exit criterion cannot pass on scheduling alone.
